mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 5.0% in a month triggers a short-term discounting effect, lowering the present value of future equities and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger month (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.0% for ≥ 30 consecutive days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) coinciding with UNRATE below 5% is associated with stronger consumer confidence and higher S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE < 5% over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS is rising and UNRATE < 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (industrial production) above the prior quarter's average predicts a 20-day positive S&P 500 return as it signals healthy economic momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat during the 3-month period of elevated HOUST growth (rolling mean).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 105 for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is expected to depress equity valuations and drive negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above 105 for the subsequent 30 trading days, and 20-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.3% in a month while FEDFUNDS remains below 4%, it signals inflation concern and a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the trigger month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE below 4% combined with a decline in PAYEMS suggests weak wage growth and consumer uncertainty, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the interaction period.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising GDPC1 (personal consumption) above 2% of previous month's value indicate sustained demand, predicting positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative during the 6-month high-GDPC1 growth window.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 10% in a month, it indicates weak retail activity and is expected to coincide with negative 20-day S&P 500 returns regardless of monetary policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the 4-month period of declining RSAFS.
